body:
**Draft.** Fills the measured results from the E0–E6 programme into the evaluation tables
and text.

> **Not compiled.** No LaTeX toolchain was available in the environment this was written
> in, so the markup needs a build before review. Structural checks only: environment and
> column counts balance.

Every number traces to a committed record in its row's own repository. Results digest with
the per-row links, including what is *not* available and why:
https://github.com/softlash/LIN-1160/blob/main/docs/RESULTS-REPORT.md

---

## Status of every experiment in the runbook

Runbook §2's experiment-to-claim matrix, plus the sub-experiments §5–§8 define separately.
**Five rows are finished, two are running, one is blocked, two were never resourced.**

| Runbook row | Priority | Status | What exists | Paper destination |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **E0** environment / parity / instrumentation gate | P0 gate | **correctness complete; evidence items open** | every correctness gate closed, 114 tests pass at tip `a7352497`, `tracked_dirty=0`, archive 22/22 | preflight + correctness appendix |
| **E1** Qwen3-4B-Base DAPO-Math GRPO, seeds 11/22/33 | P0 | **running since 2026-09-15** | correctness tests 1–2 at real 32-GPU geometry; seed 11 at rollout 470/800, held-out accuracy peaking at rollout 280 | RQ1 AR row — **pending** |
| **E2** SD3.5-M UniRL, seeds 11/22/33 | P0 | **complete** | 3 seeds × 4 quality axes + diversity; 19/19 rows, 0 errors | RQ1 diffusion row — **filled** |
| **E2-R** VeRL-Omni full-budget reference | P0 | **trained, not evaluated** | 3 seeds × 300 steps; exports audited 15/15 bit-identical | RQ1 reference column — **open** |
| **E3** UniRL vs VeRL-Omni `01c87ee5`, 8-GPU SD3.5 | P0 | **complete** | 3 replicates × 3 configurations, 10/10 runs `rc=0` | RQ2 table — **filled** |
| **§6.2** AR systems pair | P0 | **unresourced by design** | nothing; `<VERL_COMMIT>` is blank and the veRL example is a GSM8K scaffold | RQ2 AR row — runbook says **omit** |
| **E4a** lineage/group equality control | P0 | **complete, passes** | 24/24 checks in both scopes | RQ3 enablement — **filled** |
| **E4b** root- vs rewrite-scope learning | P0 | **complete, NULL** | 6 runs `rc=0`, 37 configurations scored | RQ3 — **filled as a null** |
| **E5-T** topology pair (colocated vs 4+4) | P0 minimum | **complete** | 3 replicates `rc=0`, 54/54 checksums | RQ3 — **filled** |
| **E5-R** paired representation slice | P0 minimum | **blocked** | harness audit only — the checked-in harness does not measure it | RQ3 — **open decision** |
| **E5 §7.2** broad backends / scaling / integration-effort | P2 extension | **not started** | — | RQ3 extensions |
| **E6** matched sync/async Qwen3 sweep | P1 | **pilot done, grid not run** | 6 points at 1 seed; `Q_TARGET` pilot returned a **null** | RQ4 Pareto + table — **pilot filled, grid absent** |

### E0 — gate, correctness complete

Every correctness gate is closed. Tests 1 and 2 fell to E1's measurement at real 32-GPU
geometry — mean |Δlogp| **0.01104** and **0.01543** via `TensorWeightSync`, gate unarmed,
three independent geometries agreeing to ~15%. Test 6 fell to an RNG fix: nothing under
`unirl/train/` or `unirl/distributed/` called `torch.manual_seed`, so LoRA A-matrix
initialisation drew from global RNG and two runs with different seed IDs could share an
initialisation. Gate 6 closed via `UNIRL_METRICS_JSONL`.

**Six evidence items remain, none a correctness gate** and all CPU-only work against
artifacts on disk: the PE lineage wire fix, a metrics-sink launcher edit, a root-count
assertion, the run-directory bundler (gate 1's §4 contract), the gate-7 JSONL parser, and
`parity.tsv` — which is blocked on a schema decision regardless.

E0 also wrote the **§3 `dirty.patch` capture**, which had no implementation anywhere and
existed only as prose in three documents.

### E1 — running again since 2026-09-15. The RQ1 AR row is in progress, not absent.

The row stalled for days on an evaluation-path hang; that hang is now **diagnosed, fixed
upstream, and validated at 32 devices**, and training resumed on 2026-09-15. Seed 11 is at
**rollout 470 of 800**; seeds 22 and 33 have not started. The table above is updated
accordingly, and the RQ1 AR row should be described as pending rather than omitted.

**What the row already establishes, independent of the training result:** correctness tests
1–2 at real 32-GPU geometry (above); `zero_std_group_ratio` **0.641** at rollout 0 with **no
filter configured anywhere**, so the effective batch is ~184 of 512 — a budget input nobody
had; and that **seeds govern data order, not generation** (no `random_seed` plumbing under
`unirl/rollout/`, `ARSamplingParams` has no seed field), so bit-exact seed reruns are
unavailable and reports must say so.

**The first signal, on the validation instrument rather than the primary endpoint.** Internal
AIME avg@16 over 60 held-out prompts, evaluated every 10 rollouts, **peaks at rollout 280** at
0.1260 — 6.1× the 0.0208 baseline — and then declines to a 5-point mean of 0.0867, a fall of
**−0.0314 ≈ 4.5σ**, flattening at ~0.085 for the next 100 rollouts. The dispersion is
**measured rather than assumed**: a checkpoint failure caused rollout 200 to be evaluated twice
on identical weights (0.0979 / 0.1135), giving σ ≈ 0.011, which matches the binomial standard
error on 960 samples (0.0099).

**Two limits mean this shape should not be drafted into the AR row yet, and the protocol
section already anticipates the first.** Internal AIME is secondary by design — it runs at
temperature 1.0 with an 8,192-token cap, while the prespecified primary endpoint is MATH-500
avg@4 at temperature 0.6 / top-p 0.95 with a **16,384** cap, so an AIME-selected checkpoint is
reported as validation-selected. The two are not the same measurement, and only the exports at
rollouts 200/400/600/800 will put the endpoint on a shared checkpoint set — which is the form
that made the diffusion row's comparison valid.

**Second, and unexcluded: truncation confounds this decline specifically.** The run truncates
about 30% of completions at 8,192. An evaluation extracts a final answer and a capped
completion has none, so a truncated eval completion scores wrong; since response length grows
over training, the truncation rate against a *fixed* 8,192 cap rises with it, which predicts a
falling internal accuracy with no change in capability at 16,384. (The training-side
`truncated_reward: keep` setting, which correctly rules truncation out as an explanation for
the *reward* series, does not apply to evaluation scoring.) That check has now been run. Proxy truncation
rose 0.2356 to 0.2684 between rollouts 280 and 440, a rise of 3.4 standard errors; under the
worst case that every truncated completion scores zero, the instrument accounts for **15.2%**
of the observed decline and capability for 84.8%. **The decline is therefore capability, and it
survives at about 4 standard deviations** — correcting for the cap raises the drop from 0.0333
to 0.0386 but raises its standard error in the same proportion, so the significance does not
improve. Two limits remain: the evaluation sink records neither length nor truncation rate, so
the figure above is a training-prompt proxy and the eval-side rate cannot be recovered for a
finished run; and with checkpoints every 200 rollouts the MATH-500 exports will bracket rollout
280 rather than contain it.

**On the asynchronous row's turnover, this row supports the direction and not a located peak** — different launcher, different row, and a *synchronous* run, but measured on the secondary instrument above, so it corroborates that held-out quality turns over rather than fixing where. Two limits belong with it. `save_interval`
is 200, so **rollout 280 fell between saves and the best-generalizing policy has no
artifact**; and the prespecified primary endpoint is the rollout-800 checkpoint, which on this
trajectory measures a policy past its best. That is a consequence of a fixed-budget design,
not a measurement failure.

**A label this branch's earlier revision used is withdrawn, and the corrected version is a
contrast rather than an agreement: "reward overfitting" describes the diffusion row and
neither autoregressive one.** On the diffusion row the optimised objective rises
monotonically across all six checkpoints while both frozen judges flatten over the same six
— the objective keeps improving and the external metrics do not, which is the phenomenon.
On the asynchronous row the training reward **declines across the very window on which
held-out accuracy declines**: 25-rollout window means peak at 0.4270 over rollouts 126–150
and fall monotonically to 0.3413 over 251–300, while MATH-500 goes 0.7980 → 0.7730. On this
synchronous row the reward sits in 0.358–0.387 from rollout 63 to 363 — a plateau, never an
improvement, and confirmed as one by dispersion: the highest 25-rollout window exceeds the
mean of the other eleven by 0.0202, or 1.4 standard errors, with the raw maximum falling at
rollout 323 rather than anywhere near the middle of the run. It declines only after rollout
375. **Reward overfitting requires the optimised objective to keep
improving; on the autoregressive path it does not, and on the asynchronous row it turns over
alongside held-out quality near rollout 140.** So the two modalities behave differently, and
that contrast is the reportable finding. An earlier revision of this branch asserted the
overfitting reading for the asynchronous row and stated that the diffusion row showed "the
same shape"; both are corrected.

Truncation is not a candidate explanation either: the recipe sets `truncated_reward: keep`, so
a length-capped trace is scored on its partial text rather than zeroed, and the recipe
predicts 3–5k response lengths by design, which is where the run sits at 3.9–4.4k.

**The eval-path defect, since the paper describes this system.** The driver parked at
`ar.py:489` in `score_and_attach` with every rank idle, no exception and no timeout. The stack
of the wedged rank — 1 of 384 rank dumps — is in CPython's own `_terminate_pool`
(`multiprocessing/pool.py:732`), which sends each grader child `SIGTERM` and then joins it
**with no timeout**. The hazard therefore needs a grader child that is *alive and refuses to
die*: a real grade on an expression the symbolic verifier cannot finish, inside C-level code
that never reaches a bytecode boundary. The fix removes the pool and reaps with an
uncatchable `SIGKILL` plus a bounded join
([Tencent-Hunyuan/UniRL#462](https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/UniRL/pull/462)). Validated at
32 devices: 8/8 evaluation batches at `eval_acc` 0.0208, against 0.0000 from a
deliberately-broken-grader control and 0.0219 at 8 devices.

**Two structural accounts carried in earlier revisions of this branch are superseded, and
both would have misdescribed the system.** First, that reward and rollout sharing one
strictly-serial Ray actor caused the stall: the colocation is real, but at the stall the
outstanding reward task was already `RUNNING` with nothing queued behind it, and a serial
actor predicts a bounded delay rather than an unbounded hang. Second, that asynchronous
configurations were **safe by construction** because they cannot colocate the two roles: that
followed only from the placement account being correct. The real mechanism lives in the reward
service both trainers share, and the triggering grade expiry occurs at roughly 1 per 11,000
grades — so the asynchronous runs cleared by chance rather than by construction. The fix
removes the hazard on both paths.

### E2 — complete, and the reference arm is the open part

**UniRL arm.** Full 1,632-prompt set at K=16, **26,112 images per preference row**, 19/19
rows scored with **0 errors**. Generation drift bit-identical over six hours; scorer drift
`0.000000e+00` twice, so the deltas are attributable to the adapters and nothing else.

Beyond the endpoints now in `tab:rq1`:

- **The diversity guard fired on all three seeds**, −24 to −25%, every interval far from zero.
- **The narrowing is already present at rollout 50** on all three seeds, so truncating the budget does not avoid the diversity cost — the first sixth delivers most of the gain *and* most of the narrowing.
- **Composition rises in every `atom_count` stratum**, 15,200 images, 0 errors.
- **PickScore — the optimised objective — rises monotonically at all six checkpoints while both frozen judges flatten after 150.**

**E2-R.** Three seeds × 300 steps complete, and the export path had to be written from
DTensor shards because verl's merger dies on an SD3 config with no `model_type`. Exports
audited: **15/15 consecutive checkpoint pairs on all three seeds, native == export
bit-identical** rather than merely within tolerance.

**No held-out evaluation was run, deliberately.** The estimator mismatch between the stacks
is unresolved and a head-to-head number would invite the equivalent-algorithm comparison
the runbook's gate 4 blocks. **This is the open decision on the RQ1 reference column.**

### E3 — complete. Filled, with both qualifications in the text.

Detail behind the table: medians per replicate are UniRL 63.62/64.31/64.29, SDPA
111.33/112.37/111.26, FA3 113.28/112.26/111.28. Both frameworks reproduce process-to-process
at ~1–2%. The rebuilt CUDA 13 stack is not distorting the baseline — July's 111.4/113.6
reproduce as 111.33/113.28.

**The two qualifications are in the diff rather than below it**, because each weakens the
headline: the pair is **not parameter-matched** (243 vs 191 LoRA modules, 1.27×; conservative
ratio **1.70×**), and **the median is the reported unit because the mean is unstable on one
arm** — so a reader preferring means would see a *larger* UniRL advantage.

### §6.2 AR systems pair — unresourced by design

`<VERL_COMMIT>` is deliberately blank, and the official veRL Qwen3-4B FSDP example is a
scaffold: different model variant, GSM8K rather than DAPO-Math, different group size,
response budget and KL/objective settings. Running it head-to-head would also need a second
32-GPU allocation. **The runbook's instruction where parity is impossible is to omit the row
rather than substitute a nearby recipe**, and that is what the paper should do.

### E4 — the semantic control passes; the quality comparison is a null

**E4a passes 24/24 in both scopes**, including root-shard split→concat and roots shuffled
and reconstructed by ID, with the float32 reduction bit-exact against the ID join. This is
the result that establishes retained ancestry selects a real optimization grouping.

**E4b is a null** — the seeds disagree in sign. A paired bootstrap over 64 roots on a single
seed gave root-conditioned HPSv3 **+0.387 [+0.085, +0.706]**; three seeds do not sustain it.
The binding constraint is **seed count**, not rewrite quality. Per the runbook's predeclared
interpretation, the negative result is retained rather than repaired.

Supporting work worth knowing: adapter load verified **bit-exact** (382 tensors matched, max
|Δ| 0.000e+00) rather than merely effective; the frozen AR proven un-updatable
**structurally** (no optimizer under `ar`, `_train_tracks=("diffusion",)`, `backend=None`,
`ar_sync` unbuilt); pre-registration timestamped before any rewrite-arm scoring; and the
64-root question settled by measurement — paired half-width **±0.16–0.18 HPSv3**, 4.3–4.9×
tighter than unpaired.

**The `pe`-block disclosure is in the diff** because it is needed to interpret the measured
arm: 71% of rewrites carry chat markers, 73% exceed CLIP's 77-token window, 0/256 have the
marker. The fix was committed and deliberately unapplied so the measured rows stay
attributable to one configuration.

### E5 — E5-T complete, E5-R blocked, extensions not started

**E5-T** is in the diff. Two points the record insists on and the text now carries: the
**2.277× may not be attributed to `layout`** (the phase breakdown is the deliverable), and
**under separate topology UniRL is slower than VeRL-Omni colocated** — 146.244 s against
111.33 — which is the sentence to lead with.

**E5-R is blocked and it is a design decision, not pending work.** The runbook's §7.2
requires a paired slice over the *same recorded E4 tensors, device, transport and operations*
for tree versus `flat_id_join` with exact E4a semantics. The checked-in harness does not
measure that. Three design choices are open; the decision is whether to build a correct
E5-R by joining the CPU oracle to the GPU timer, or to narrow RQ3 to the topology result.

**§7.2's broader work** — same/cross-GPU and cross-node backends across `colocate_store`,
`gpu_store` and `transfer_queue`, strong and weak scaling, and the held-out
integration-effort study — is a P2 extension and has not started. Cross-node work needs a
multi-node allocation. RDMA is present on our pods, so it is not hardware-blocked.

**The CPU trajectory-IR timings already in the paper** are generated and archived with 100
per-cell raw trials and SHA-256 checksums. They are single-process regression measurements,
not distributed or GPU throughput, and the manuscript already says so.

### E6 — pilot filled, grid absent, and the pilot changed the grid's design

The capacity pilot's six per-rollout rates are in the diff. **The `Q_TARGET` pilot failed
its own preregistered rule, so no threshold is registered** — and that is a result about the
training dynamics rather than a missing number.

**Two things gate the formal grid, and the runbook's own §8.2 is why one of them matters.**

1. **The six §6.3 buffer counters are unwritten.** §6.3 requires complete per-step series for admitted, carried, suspended, **rejected**, discarded, retried and completed work. `rejected` — the mechanism bounded staleness acts through — is constructed each step by `keep_within_lag` and **never counted**; `discarded` goes to `logger.info`; `retried` has no concept in `unirl/rollout/`. §12's expected result leans on rejection rising with lag and **that series does not exist**. This blocks admissibility on 15 of 18 runs.
2. **S0 was blocked by the evaluation-path defect above, and is unblocked as of 2026-09-15.** §12's first named primary contrast, **S0 vs D0 (allocation/residency)**, is therefore back in reach rather than deferred, and its runs are independent of the rest, so nothing already priced is redone. **D0 vs A1, the question RQ4 actually asks, was never affected.**

**Gate 4's mandatory §8.1 correction is done.** The stock sync/async pair differs in five
fields that affect the estimator or learner execution — `normalize_adv_by_std`, the high
clipping bound, loss aggregation, attention implementation and the microplanner — and the
grid forces one value for each with explicit overrides. `tab:sync-async-preflight` already
records this.

**Also measured and worth the manuscript's attention:** `perf/step_time_s` **understates an
eval iteration by 3.9×** (133.32 against 519.06, with phase timers summing to within 3 ms),
and ~1.3× run-level at `eval_interval: 10`. §3's prose claim about that field is now
measured; both figures should be quoted, labelled.

---

## The evidence-admission gates (§1), as they stand

| Gate | Status |
|---|---|
| 1 source identity | **closed** — E0 wrote the `dirty.patch` capture that had no implementation; two false-evidence traps found and fixed (`git diff` cannot see untracked files; `on_remote=0` is distinct from dirty and worse) |
| 2 resolved configuration | **closed with a caveat** — UniRL's Hydra outputs escape run directories, so per-run archiving misses them; the remedy is the commit plus archived launch overrides, and a launcher records what it was *told*, not what it ran |
| 3 input identity | **closed** — data sha256s, model and evaluator revisions archived per row |
| 4 semantic parity | **closed for E3 and E6's grid**; the E2-R head-to-head is blocked *by* this gate |
| 5 correctness before speed | **closed** — tests 1, 2 and 6 |
| 6 raw evidence | **closed, and it paid for itself** — the `gz-8` pod was reclaimed ~9 h after E4 copied its artifacts off; everything remained readable, and no published figure was lost |
| 7 regeneration | **partly open** — the run-directory bundler and gate-7 JSONL parser are two of E0's six remaining items |

---

## Still open, with the `TODO[data]` notes now naming which

The four generic `TODO[data]` markers are replaced with specific ones. In short: E1's AR row
(running — seed 11 at rollout 470/800, seeds 22/33 not started), E2-R's reference column (trained and audited, not evaluated), E5-R (harness does
not measure it), RQ2 scaling (deferred by design), and the E6 grid — **whose pilot produced a
null rather than a bounded-staleness conclusion, so E6 should not be mentioned in the
abstract on present evidence.**

## Two limits that touch how any of these numbers may be read

**At three seeds a *t* interval carries 2 degrees of freedom** and is wide by construction.
The means are precise — 26,112 prompts per preference row, 800 per composition row, zero
scoring errors — but every dispersion is n=3 and carries ±50% relative sampling error, so
per-seed values are reported rather than a standard deviation.

**An evaluation-noise floor limits every checkpoint comparison.** Two independent scorings
of the *same* checkpoint differ by 0.40 aggregate accuracy points but **agree on only
380/500 prompts**; `--random-seed` does not pin per-request sampling. **No per-prompt,
per-subset or per-difficulty claim from a single scoring is reliable** — aggregate stability
comes from averaging, not from sampling repeatability.

title: Fill measured experiment results into the evaluation section
